result:
No. Redis solves cross-process and cross-host coordination, and you have neither. A single writer means no contention to arbitrate, and SQLite already gives you durability plus boot recovery. Adding Redis buys you a second source of truth, a network hop, and a new failure domain that takes the service down when it is unreachable.

The Elixir runtime already covers what Redis would be doing here: GenServer state for the hot path, ETS for shared reads, `:persistent_term` for config-shaped data that rarely changes. All of it in-process, no serialization, no network.

Revisit if one of these becomes true: you run more than one node and they need shared state, you need pub/sub or a work queue with competing consumers across hosts, or the working set outgrows what you want resident in the BEAM heap. Until then the SQLite plus in-process design is the simpler correct one.
